decisions.reason: Message 176 already independently introduces the food-contact material standard with FOOD_SERVICE scope; the service-access scope change adds nothing further.
The existing message-176 MODIFY already captures sanitation access, liquid-trap prevention, and FOOD_SERVICE scope for the dispensing path.
Extending internal component service access to the food-service context does not change the machine's structural stability or vibration requirements.
The existing message-176 MODIFY already adds FOOD_SERVICE scope to liquid-electrical isolation; no additional update or removal is required.
The existing message-176 MODIFY already extends removable-whisk behavior to cleaning and retail food-service use.
The existing message-176 MODIFY already captures cleaning and retail food-service scope for removable bowls.
Food-service maintenance access does not necessarily change the milestone-local strategy of using off-the-shelf electrical components.
The service-access context extension does not entail a change to the accepted enclosure size or form factor.
Message 176 already separately adds CAD-file retention; the service-access scope change does not require another change to the layout or CAD deliverable.
Message 176 already separately adds wiring-layout retention, and the service-access scope extension does not otherwise alter the wiring-plan requirement.
Maintenance access and food-service applicability do not necessarily alter the spout's geometry, orientation, material, or pour direction.

The source decision does not require a new BOM or change any selected component; its documentation request names materials, CAD, wiring, cleaning procedures, and exploded views rather than altering the BOM state.
